questions.problem:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of $T,$ where $T$ is defined as

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}\,\,v \\ u+{v}^{2}\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

 

To find the locations of the critical points of $T,$ we need to solve 

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}=0.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)={u}^{2}\,\,v$ and $y(u,v)=u+{v}^{2}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =2uv & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & ={u}^{2} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =1 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =2v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2uv & {u}^{2} \\ 1 & 2v\end{aligned}| \\  & =2uv\cdot 2v-{u}^{2}\cdot 1 \\  & =4u{v}^{2}-{u}^{2} \\  & =u(4{v}^{2}-u).\end{aligned}
$$

The function has critical points when $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}=0.$ So, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =0 \\ u(4{v}^{2}-u) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equation $u(4{v}^{2}-u)=0$ defines a pair of intersecting curves in the $uv$-plane: the line $u=0$ and the parabola $u=4{v}^{2}.$

questions.problem:
Consider the transformation $T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)).$ The inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}(x,y)\to (u(x,y),v(x,y))$ is given by

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x-y \\ x+2y\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the Jacobian determinant of $T.$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)},$ the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}.$

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1}.
$$

Here, we have $u(x,y)=2x-y$ and $v(x,y)=x+2y.$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =2 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =-1 \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & =1 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot 1 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & ={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation $T,$ where $T$ is defined as

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}-{v}^{2} \\ uv\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the locations of the critical points of $T,$ we need to solve 

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}=0.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)={u}^{2}-{v}^{2}$ and $y(u,v)=uv.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =2u & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =-2v \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =v & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =u\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2u & -2v \\ v & u\end{aligned}| \\  & =2u\cdot u-(-2v)\cdot v \\  & =2{u}^{2}+2{v}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The function has critical points when $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}=0.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =0 \\ 2({u}^{2}+{v}^{2}) & =0 \\ {u}^{2}+{v}^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation ${u}^{2}+{v}^{2}=0$ defines the point $(0,0)$ in the $uv$-plane.

questions.problem:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation $T,$ where $T$ is defined as

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}(u-1)^{3}-(v-2)^{3} \\ u+v\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the locations of the critical points of $T,$ we need to solve 

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}=0.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=(u-1)^{3}-(v-2)^{3}$ and $y(u,v)=u+v.$  

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =3(u-1)^{2} & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =-3(v-2)^{2} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =1 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3(u-1)^{2} & -3(v-2)^{2} \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(u-1)^{2}\cdot 1-(-3(v-2)^{2})\cdot 1 \\  & =3(u-1)^{2}+3(v-2)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The function has critical points when $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}=0.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =0 \\ 3(u-1)^{2}+3(v-2)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation $3(u-1)^{2}+3(v-2)^{2}=0$ defines the point $(1,2)$ in the $uv$-plane.
